solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Member holding head of orchid with a distinctive smell

indicators.note: the limb word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: an arm is a member, a limb of the body

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone clutching an orchid bloom that gives off a strong scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts O, from 'head of orchid', inside ARM; then the clue's own 'a' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a distinctive smell, especially a pleasant one, is an aroma.

clue.text: Simon perhaps having job holding drink? The opposite!

indicators.note: one word holds another inside it
says the containment is the other way round from how the clue first reads, so the drink holds the job

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
a post is a job, a position

explanation.surface: Someone called Simon has a job that involves holding a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, the job word would hold the drink; 'The opposite!' flips which piece goes inside which.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Simon Peter was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Seemingly vandalised that one office

indicators.note: something vandalised has been smashed up, so these letters are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: Apparently one particular office has been vandalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vandalised' rearranges the thirteen letters of THAT ONE OFFICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a phrase meaning judging by appearances, which is what seemingly means.

clue.text: An aperitif? A favourite is brought in for each

indicators.note: the favourite and 'is' are brought inside the next piece

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an aperitif is served to each favoured guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in' signals containment; 'for each' is one Latin-derived word, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pre-dinner drink is one kind of thing taken to whet the appetite, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Article quite new — not this then!

parts.note: 'an' is the indefinite article in grammar

indicators.note: the letters are made new, put into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone notes that an item is quite new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges QUITE into TIQUE. The definition plays on the surface: if an article is antique, it is certainly not new.
explanation.definitionFit: Antithesis: an old collectable piece is the opposite of something new, which is what 'this' refers to.

clue.text: Dope about fixed property

indicators.note: the fool word goes around the next piece

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
set means fixed, as in set in stone

explanation.surface: A drug sold around fixed property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' splits the fool word so the second piece sits between its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: things owned that have value, a person's or firm's possessions, are its holdings.

clue.text: Bill shot when heading off

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, of the word goes

parts.note: a stab is a shot, an attempt, as in have a stab at it

explanation.surface: Someone settles the bill when heading off from a bar after a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the S from STAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in a pub or restaurant, the running account owed is the tab, the bill.

clue.text: Army officer taking pity on merchant ship's skipper

parts.note: to give quarter is to show mercy or pity to an enemy
the captain of a merchant vessel is called its master

explanation.surface: An army officer shows mercy to the captain of a trading vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this officer is responsible for an army unit's stores and supplies.

clue.text: Relaxed without difficulty

definitions.meaning: without difficulty means simple to do

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: calm and unworried, and simple to do, both covered by the same adjective.

clue.text: Cops out, deployed to find sea creature

indicators.note: things deployed are arranged and spread out, so these letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Police are sent out to locate a marine animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this eight-armed mollusc lives in the sea.

clue.text: Money that is missing from old golf club

indicators.note: the second piece goes missing from the first

parts.note: a brassie was an old wooden golf club, roughly a two-wood
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Cash has disappeared from an old golf club's funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing from' removes IE from BRASSIE. 'Old golf club' reads as a clubhouse but is a hickory-era club.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: in Britain brass is informal for cash, as in 'where there's muck there's brass'.

clue.text: Form of cricket in Tokyo Olympics year

definitions.meaning: the short twenty-overs-a-side cricket format, T20
the Tokyo Olympics were scheduled for 2020

explanation.surface: A cricket format appears at the Tokyo Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the short twenty-overs cricket game, and the year written as two pairs of digits.

clue.text: Watch programme that includes ad for beauty aid?

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it

indicators.note: the programme word takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: a show is a programme on TV

explanation.surface: Someone watches a TV programme featuring an advert for a cosmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' places the advert inside the programme word; 'Watch' is a verb, not a timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: coloured powder for the eyelids is one kind of cosmetic, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Last of intake failing to pass

indicators.note: the last letter of the following word

parts.note: a lapse is a failing, a slip

explanation.surface: The last student admitted fails to pass an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: time passes or goes by, said of a period that runs out.

clue.text: Stuff about English and their patron saint

indicators.note: the eating word goes around the next piece

parts.note: to gorge or stuff oneself is to overeat

explanation.surface: Someone gorges on English food and tales of England's saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside GORGE. 'their' points back to the English.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Saint George, the dragon-slayer, is England's patron saint.

clue.text: Remove from superfluous court

parts.note: extra means surplus to requirements

explanation.surface: Someone is removed from a court deemed superfluous.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to extract something is to pull it out or take it away.

clue.text: Heads of stores take in goods, marketing a brand

indicators.note: the heads, the first letters, of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Store bosses take in goods while marketing a brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads of' takes the first letters of five words, then 'a' is added as it stands. 'brand' looks commercial but means a mark of shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a brand in the sense of a mark of disgrace is a stigma.

clue.text: Candid conversation in centre — try feeding toddler afterwards

indicators.note: the toddler part comes after the centre part

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre

indicators.note: one piece feeds into, goes inside, the other

parts.note: a tot is a small child
a judge hears or tries a case

explanation.surface: A frank chat at a nursery while trying to feed a toddler afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feeding' puts the try word inside the toddler word, and 'afterwards' places that after the centre word. 'try' is the legal sense: a judge hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a frank and intimate talk between two people is described this way.

clue.text: Prima donna keen to come over

indicators.note: to come over is to turn over, so the word is read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: avid means keen, eager

explanation.surface: An opera star is eager to come and visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a leading female opera singer, or a temperamental star, is a diva.

clue.text: Conclude there's no escaping from hell

indicators.note: the word 'no' escapes, leaves, the hell word

parts.note: an inferno is a hell, a raging fire

explanation.surface: Someone decides there is no way out of hell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escaping from' takes NO out of INFERNO.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to deduce something from evidence is to conclude it.

clue.text: Manage to go

definitions.meaning: to go quickly on foot is to ..., as a machine ... or goes

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to be in charge of something, and to move or operate, share one verb.

clue.text: Turn tide somehow at a plant

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in it's your go

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged in some unspecified way

explanation.surface: Someone turns the tide somehow at a plant, like a power station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges the letters of 'tide'; 'Turn' is a noun here, a go in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an annual flowering garden species, also called clarkia, from western North America.

clue.text: A new girl returned after short time for aerial

indicators.note: the girl comes after the time letter

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: the girl's name comes back, read backwards

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A new girl came back after a short time for an aerial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns ANNE into ENNA; 'short time' is the abbreviation T.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a radio or TV aerial is also called an antenna.

clue.text: Most unpleasant defeat

definitions.meaning: the superlative of bad, the most unpleasant
to ... an opponent is to beat them

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the superlative of bad, and an old verb meaning to get the better of someone.
